Hi Carla —

Really appreciate the annotated doc; good questions. High-level answers below (I summarized so your legal/procurement team can paste into the SIG). I've attached a compact matrix that maps each SIG section to "Hosted / Dedicated / Private (VPC/on-prem)" responsibilities.

1) Backups, logs, metrics (Dedicated):
- Default: in Dedicated, runtime data (inference requests, tokenized payloads) are served from the customer's dedicated GPU pool and ephemeral nodes. However, control-plane telemetry (aggregated metrics, billing events) is retained by Redwood by default for operational purposes.
- Option: customers can opt into a Dedicated isolation policy where control-plane telemetry is forwarded to customer-managed storage and we disable retention in Redwood-managed buckets. This is a provisioning-time configuration and is documented in our Dedicated onboarding checklist.

2) Private (VPC / on-prem) KMS patterns:
- Private VPC: we support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) where encryption keys never leave the customer's cloud KMS. By default we do not escrow keys for Private VPC deployments.
- On-prem air-gapped installs: customer controls keys; Redwood provides integration adapters. If a customer requests escrow for managed key recovery, that is handled under a separate enterprise agreement and explicit controls (not default).

3) Hosted and PII flow statement (short):
- "Hosted API: inference request payloads are processed in Redwood-hosted infrastructure. We do not persist raw request payloads longer than 7 days by default, and customers can enable further retention limits or opt for Dedicated/Private deployments where data residency is controlled by the customer. Redwood does not access customer-provided keys in Hosted mode."

Next steps: Jonas, can you add two quick technical notes for the SIG: (a) how KV/prefix caching is handled in Dedicated and (b) what log ingestion paths look like for the isolation option? I can then push a one-page SIG addendum to you.

Feel free to propose 30-min times; I'm available tomorrow afternoon.

Best,

Carla — quick technical follow-up, adding specifics you can paste into the SIG.

On Thu, May 14, 2026 at 09:12 AM Carla Reyes <carla.reyes@medtechinc.com> wrote:
> - In your spreadsheet you marked "Dedicated" as "customer data isolated" — can you confirm whether backups, logs, and metrics can still be routed to Redwood-managed buckets in the hosted control plane, or are those fully customer-managed for Dedicated?

Answer (Dedicated):
- Runtime inference traffic: served from tenant-specific GPU pools; no cross-tenant request paths.
- Backups: model weights and snapshots are stored in dedicated customer buckets when configured; default snapshot retention is configurable. If you enable the "full customer-managed storage" toggle during provisioning, Redwood will not copy snapshots to our managed buckets.
- Logs & metrics: two categories — (1) Operational telemetry (node health, scheduler metrics) and (2) Request-level logs.
  - Operational telemetry: by default sent to Redwood telemetry pipeline (aggregated, sampled) to meet SLAs. Optionally, this can be forwarded to customer-managed endpoints (S3, GCS) via a delivery connector configured at onboarding.
  - Request-level logs: we mark request-level logging as "off" by default for Dedicated; it must be explicitly enabled by the customer. When enabled, request logs can be routed to customer-managed storage.

On the caching question: KV/prefix caching runs in the serving layer on the Dedicated pool nodes. Cached KV is ephemeral and bound to the serving instances; it is never persisted to the control plane. That means cache content does not leave Dedicated runtime unless a customer-specified cache-archive option is enabled.

Key management (Private):
- Private VPC and on-prem installs integrate with customer KMS (BYOK) via standard cloud KMS APIs or HSMs for on-prem. We surface a KMS abstraction in our private control plane; Redwood never has access to customer private keys when BYOK is enabled.

Evidence pointers to include in the SIG: 
- SOC 2 certificate (link): https://redwood.ai/compliance/soc2-2025.pdf
- KMS integration note: see attached kms_integration_note.txt (includes API call examples and example IAM policy snippets)

If you want, we can redact and share a sample Dedicated onboarding checklist that shows the toggle locations for "full customer-managed storage" and request-log toggles.
